assumptions: slab edge away from plate ends

TA3FF.regime: inserted length strictly between 0 and the plate length (edge away from plate ends)

TAC6D.regime: inserted length strictly between 0 and the plate length (edge away from plate ends)

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: TE652 and TBFE0 say only that the further 350 V battery is 'connected in series with the battery', not that it faces the same way; the certified wiring V + q assumes aiding polarity, while an opposing battery gives V - q (150 V, 0.0675 mN).

counterexamples: TE652 at q = 350 V with the further battery reversed: |V - q| = 150 V, F = 0.5 x 150^2 x 6e-9 N/V^2 = 0.0675 mN, not the certified 2.1675 mN; at q = 700 V reversed: 200 V, F = 0.12 mN, not 4.32 mN.
notes: Arithmetic checked: dC/dx = 600 pF/0.1 m = 6e-9 F/m; F = 3e-9 V^2: 500 V -> 0.75 mN, 650 V -> 1.2675, 850 V -> 2.1675, 1200 V -> 4.32 mN; all certified values follow under aiding polarity. Unlike sibling items, these sentences omit 'facing the same way'. The authors label the inserted length K (irrelevant while 0 < q < ell); I called it C in pass 1; both readings give the same invariant answer and I accept K. Regime 'q < ell' should strictly also require the edge away from the far end and q > 0, but all listed values (2.5, 4.5, 6.5 cm) are well inside. Minimal pairs (T09BD/TBFE0, TABCB/TE652) share 350 V and differ in attachment. TBFE0 also implicitly requires the further battery to remain connected after insertion, which 'is connected ... before the slab is inserted' supports.
